title: Warranty replacement offer
text:
Subject: Ticket KL-48213 - Warranty replacement for pump unit

Dear Mr Kowalczyk,

Thank you for your patience. Our engineers have confirmed that the motor in your pump unit failed because of a manufacturing fault, so the repair is covered by warranty. We can offer two solutions. Option A is a like-for-like replacement, shipped from our Cork depot and arriving within five working days. Option B is a newer model with a quieter motor; it ships from our Rotterdam depot and takes ten working days. If your line cannot stop for more than a week, Option A is the safer choice. Please reply by Tuesday so we can reserve the stock.

Kind regards,
Ines Moreau
Keldra Equipment Support

questions.q: Which replacement could reach the customer within a week?
options: The same as the broken item
To explain why the warranty has expired
To ask for the pump to be returned
To announce a price rise for spare motors
questions.explanation: Option A, the like-for-like replacement, arrives within five working days.

questions.q: Why was this message written?
options: The model with the quieter motor
Either unit, if payment is made on Tuesday
To present two fixes for a faulty unit
Neither one, until engineers visit
questions.explanation: It sets out Option A and Option B as warranty solutions for the failed motor.

questions.q: In the message, what does "like-for-like" mean?
options: Priced the same as the newer model
Sent by the same courier as before
Offered to a similar customer
Identical to the old item
questions.explanation: Option A is described as a replacement for the same pump, as opposed to the newer model in Option B.

title: Rebooking after cancelled flight
text:
Subject: Your cancelled flight to Lisbon, ticket TA-48213

Dear Mr Alvarez,

Please accept our apologies for the disruption. Your flight on Friday was cancelled by the airline, which has not said when the route will resume.

We are holding a seat for you on Tuesday's 18:40 departure. Please note that this hold is not a booking. We can only issue the new ticket once the airline has released your original fare, which it expects to do by noon on Monday. Only after that can we waive our change fee and claim back the unused hotel night.

There is nothing to pay for now. If you have heard nothing by 14:00 on Monday, reply to this message with the ticket number and we will chase the airline directly.

Kind regards,
Sofia Marek
Brightfield Travel Desk

questions.q: Why does Sofia stress that the hold is 'not a booking'?

She wants him to pay the change fee before the seat is lost.
She does not want him to assume the Tuesday seat is secured.
She doubts that he really wants to travel again on Tuesday.
questions.explanation: She says the new ticket can only be issued after the airline releases the original fare, so the seat is not yet secured.

The hotel night has already been refunded to the traveller and the agency.
A deposit must be paid today to keep the Tuesday seat for him.
The airline plans to restart the route again at the start of next week.

title: Refund approved, new date

Subject: Your refund request, ticket KL-48213

Camille Dufour

title: Supply alert: Belgian strike
text:
SUPPLY ALERT - Possible delays in Belgium

A national transport strike is expected to run from Wednesday 11 November to Friday 13 November, and carriers anticipate knock-on disruption well into the following week. Deliveries to and from the Ghent site may therefore slip by two to four days, although road freight from the Netherlands should be largely unaffected. We would be grateful if customers could confirm by 17:00 on Monday 9 November whether any orders due that week should be rerouted to the Antwerp depot; after that time, loads will be released in the original sequence and no further changes can be accepted. Orders already in transit will not be recalled. Questions should go to Aisha Rahman in Planning, who is coordinating the response with Omar Haddad in Transport.

To tell customers to order earlier this month.

Planners are sending forecasts that are too low.
Customers are ordering from other carriers.
The holiday will cause a shortage of stock.

Send their forecasts to the warehouse on Friday 28.
Ask Beatriz to approve extra warehouse hours.
Check forecasts and order by Wednesday noon.

title: Cartons delayed two weeks
text:
SUPPLY ALERT - Cartons for Line 4 delayed by two weeks

Marlowe Cargo has advised that the corrugated cartons for Line 4 will arrive on 23 November rather than the original 9 November, owing to a customs hold at the border. Planners covering secondary packaging are asked to review every open order that depends on this material and to flag any that cannot be rescheduled without breaching customer commitments. Hannah will consolidate the findings and present them at the supply review on Thursday 12 November, so submissions must reach her no later than two working days before the review. Yuki is arranging an interim batch of smaller cartons from an alternative source, but this stock is limited and will be allocated only to orders already marked as urgent. Questions should go to Camille at the Nottingham site.

questions.q: Who is expected to compile the planners' findings?
options: Hannah, before the review
Yuki, once the alternative stock arrives
Camille, on behalf of the Nottingham site
The carrier, after the customs hold ends
questions.explanation: Hannah will consolidate the findings and present them at the supply review.

questions.q: By what date must planners send their findings?
options: Thursday 12 November
Monday 9 November
Monday 23 November
Tuesday 10 November
questions.explanation: The review is on Thursday 12 November, and the submissions are due two working days earlier.

questions.q: Which statement is consistent with the notice?
options: The interim cartons can be used for any affected order.
The delay comes from a shortage at the supplier's own plant.
Yuki is the person who must review all of the open orders.
Only orders marked as urgent can use the substitute stock.
questions.explanation: The interim batch is limited and allocated only to orders already marked as urgent.

title: Order entry weekend downtime
text:
SERVICE NOTICE: Order entry offline this weekend
The order system will be down from Friday 18:00 until Monday 06:00 for a planned upgrade, so you cannot enter or change orders. Orders confirmed in the system before 16:00 on Friday will go to the warehouse as usual; anything unconfirmed will wait until Monday. For urgent orders, email the Frankfurt warehouse desk and we will key them in by hand once the system is back.
Thank you for your understanding.
Elena Vogt, Norvia Packaging

questions.q: What must planners do for their Friday orders to reach the warehouse as usual?
options: Confirm them in the system before 16:00
Email them to the warehouse desk
Enter them again after 06:00 on Monday
Wait until 18:00 and then confirm them
questions.explanation: Only orders confirmed before 16:00 on Friday are released as usual.

questions.q: In the notice, what does 'key them in' mean?
options: check them against the forecast
send them out to customers
type them into the system
cancel them until Monday
questions.explanation: The desk enters the emailed orders by hand once the system is back.

title: Cold storage unit alert
text:
SUPPLY ALERT: Cold storage unit 4

On Tuesday at 06:15 the temperature alarm in unit 4 at the Rotterdam port terminal started. A cooling fan had stopped, and engineers fixed it by 09:00. However, the temperature may have been too high before the repair, so every pallet inside must be checked before it is released. Aisha will check pallets that arrived before Monday. Fatima will check pallets that arrived on Monday or later. Please do not move anything out of unit 4 until Sofia sends the release email.

questions.q: Which statement is NOT true?
options: Aisha is checking part of the stock in unit 4.
Staff must wait for an email before moving pallets.
The alarm started early in the morning.
The engineers still have to repair the fan.
questions.explanation: The notice says engineers fixed the fan by 09:00.

questions.q: Which statement matches the notice?
options: Aisha will check every pallet in the unit.
Sofia will check the pallets that came before Monday.
Pallets from Monday are checked by Aisha.
Fatima checks pallets received on Monday or later.
questions.explanation: Fatima checks pallets that arrived on Monday or later.

questions.q: Why do the pallets need to be checked?
options: The alarm turned out to be a false warning.
The pallets arrived much later than planned.
The unit may have been too warm before the fix.
The engineers are still waiting for a spare part.
questions.explanation: The notice says the temperature may have been too high before the repair.

title: Stock freeze notice
text:
STOCK FREEZE - Södertälje site

From Thursday 12 to Saturday 14 November, no stock adjustments can be made in the system. Warehouse staff should finish all corrections by Wednesday evening. Last-minute corrections have caused problems before. Hannah's team will count the stock during the freeze. We know this is not convenient, and we would be grateful for your help.

questions.q: Who needs to finish the corrections by Wednesday evening?
options: Hannah's counting team
Lucas, the planner
The system supplier
The warehouse staff
questions.explanation: The notice says warehouse staff should finish all corrections by Wednesday evening.

questions.q: Why was this notice written?
options: To announce a new method of counting stock in the warehouse
To warn staff that stock changes will stop for a few days
To ask for extra staff to work on Saturday at the site
To report mistakes that were found in the stock system
questions.explanation: It explains that no adjustments can be made from Thursday to Saturday.

title: Port congestion alert
text:
Supply alert: Rotterdam port congestion

Vessel waiting times at Rotterdam have risen to six days, and we expect the delay to last until at least the end of November. To protect delivery dates, Calder & Finch asks customers to book export slots ten days ahead instead of the usual five. The earlier cut-off does not apply to temperature-controlled containers, which keep their priority berths, unless the booking is amended after the cut-off. Rafael's team at the Ghent site will confirm space within one working day. Please don't wait for the situation to improve; slots are going fast.

questions.q: What does the last sentence suggest about the company's view?
options: The congestion will probably end within days.
Customers have been booking far too early.
The port will soon stop accepting bookings.
Waiting for improvements would be a mistake.
questions.explanation: "Don't wait for the situation to improve" and "slots are going fast" show it considers delay risky.

questions.q: Which statement matches the text?
options: All containers must now be booked five days ahead.
Cooled containers are exempt unless changed late.
Rafael will confirm space within ten days.
Waiting times at the port have fallen to six days.
questions.explanation: The ten-day rule excludes temperature-controlled containers, except when amended after the cut-off.

questions.q: Which statement is NOT true?
options: Rafael's team will reply within five working days.
Vessels are currently waiting about six days.
Bookings are normally made five days ahead.
The congestion could last until the end of November.
questions.explanation: The text says Rafael's team confirms space within one working day.

title: Supply alert: ingredient X-12
text:
SUPPLY ALERT: Ingredient X-12

Our supplier's Södertälje site will close for maintenance from 4 to 18 November. We hold about three weeks of stock, so we are not worried yet, but the restart date may slip. Tomasz will call the supplier every Wednesday. Please hold new orders for X-12 until Ingrid confirms the plan.

questions.q: In this notice, what does 'slip' mean?
options: happen later than planned
be cancelled completely
come earlier than expected
stay exactly the same
questions.explanation: The writer is concerned about the restart date, so 'slip' means it could be delayed.

questions.q: Why is the company 'not worried yet'?
options: Its stock should last about three weeks.
The shutdown will be over within two or three days.
Another supplier can deliver X-12 immediately.
Tomasz has already received a firm restart date.
questions.explanation: The notice says 'We hold about three weeks of stock', which covers the two-week closure.

questions.q: Which of these is NOT part of the notice?
options: The closure begins on 4 November for maintenance work.
Tomasz will contact the supplier once a week, on Wednesdays.
New orders for X-12 should go to Ingrid today.
The restart may happen later than the supplier planned.
questions.explanation: Ingrid only confirms the plan; the notice asks people to hold new orders, not send them to her.

title: Label stock allocation
text:
SUPPLY ALERT - Label stock allocation
Vantis Labels cannot meet full demand for thermal shipping labels until the end of the year, because a coating line at our supplier failed in September. The first plan, issued on 29 September, gave every centre 40 percent of its usual order. That plan has been withdrawn. From Wednesday 4 November, available rolls will be shared by last quarter's shipping volume: Europe 55 percent, the Americas 30 percent and Asia 15 percent. The Warsaw distribution centre will handle the European share, and Pavel will confirm weekly quantities each Friday. Camille must approve any request for extra rolls, but regions do not need to submit a new forecast.

questions.q: Which statement is NOT true under the current plan?
options: Europe receives the largest share of the rolls
Each centre gets 40 percent of its normal order
Camille has to approve every request for extra rolls
The Warsaw centre handles the European allocation
questions.explanation: The 40 percent rule belonged to the first plan, which 'has been withdrawn'.

questions.q: What is the main purpose of the notice?
options: To announce that the company is changing its label supplier
To ask every region to submit a new demand forecast
To apologise to customers for a late delivery of labels
To explain how limited stock will be divided
questions.explanation: It sets out how scarce rolls will be shared among Europe, the Americas and Asia.

questions.q: Why is there not enough label stock?
options: A supplier's coating line broke down
A strike closed the Warsaw distribution centre in autumn
Demand for labels fell sharply across the Asian region
Customs inspections held up all shipments in Europe
questions.explanation: The text says a coating line at the supplier failed in September.

title: Portal sign-in change
text:
PORTAL NOTICE - New sign-in method from 1 December

To strengthen account security, the Marlowe Cargo shipping portal will replace passwords with single sign-on through your company's own identity system. We would appreciate it if each customer's account administrator could send us the names of staff who need continued access by Friday 20 November; anyone not on the list will be locked out when the switch takes place. Individual users need not do anything beforehand, and booking history will carry over unchanged. Our team in Guadalajara, led by Kenji Ito, will run test sessions on request, while Ingrid Moen handles any enquiries about access rights.

questions.q: Why is the portal changing how people sign in?
options: To merge two customer databases
To make accounts more secure
To lower the cost of password resets
To remove old booking history
questions.explanation: The notice says the change is to strengthen account security.

questions.q: Who has to send in the list of staff who need access?
options: Each customer's account administrator
Kenji Ito's team in Guadalajara
Every individual user
Ingrid Moen, who deals with access rights
questions.explanation: The administrator of each customer's account is asked to send the names.

title: Earlier dispatch cut-off
text:
Dispatch update: Nottingham site

From Monday 2 November, the cut-off for same-day dispatch moves from 16:00 to 14:30. Orders confirmed after that time will go out the next working day, unless a team leader flags them as urgent. The change follows a run of late pickups, when drivers sat at the dock while pallets were still being wrapped. Rafael has agreed the new slot with the carrier. I know this will be a pain for Sales, but we simply can't keep missing collection windows. Noah will circulate the updated cut-off table on Friday.

questions.q: Why was the cut-off brought forward?
options: The carrier started charging extra fees for evening pickups.
Collections kept being missed because loads were not ready.
Fewer people work at the site in the afternoon.
Sales asked for a simpler schedule.
questions.explanation: Drivers waited at the dock while pallets were still being wrapped.

questions.q: What does the writer imply about the change?
options: Some colleagues will dislike it, but it is seen as unavoidable.
It is temporary and will soon be reversed.
It was brought in without any prior contact with the carrier team.
It will make life easier for Sales.
questions.explanation: 'A pain for Sales' but 'we simply can't keep missing collection windows'.

questions.q: Who will share the updated cut-off table?
options: Rafael
The carrier
Noah
A team leader
questions.explanation: Noah will circulate the table on Friday.

title: New pickup days
text:
Carrier Update: New Pickup Days for the Czech Region
Ridgeway Cold Chain will change its collection days for Czech addresses from Monday 2 November. Pickups will move from Monday and Thursday to Tuesday and Friday, in order to combine routes and reduce empty mileage. We would appreciate it if you could confirm your standing orders for the new pattern by Wednesday 28 October, as route planning will be locked on that day. Standing orders that have not been confirmed will stay on the old days for one more week and will then be charged as ad-hoc pickups, at a higher rate. If your dispatch windows cannot accommodate Tuesday or Friday, please speak to Greta before the deadline.
Dev and Greta, Prague service centre

questions.q: Why does the carrier say it 'would appreciate' a confirmation?
options: The confirmation is actually needed by a fixed date.
The confirmation is only a favour and can be skipped.
The carrier wants opinions on the new days.
The carrier is unsure whether the new days will work.
questions.explanation: Route planning is locked on 28 October, so the polite request is really a deadline.

questions.q: What should a customer do if Tuesday or Friday pickups are impossible?
options: Wait until 2 November and then phone the depot.
Switch to ad-hoc pickups straight away.
Confirm the old days with Dev.
Contact Greta before 28 October.
questions.explanation: The notice says to speak to Greta before the deadline of Wednesday 28 October.

questions.q: Which statement matches the notice?
options: Unconfirmed orders keep the old days for a week.
Pickups will take place three times a week.
Ad-hoc pickups are cheaper than standing orders.
Route planning stays open after 28 October.
questions.explanation: Unconfirmed standing orders stay on the old days for one more week.

title: Stock count closure
text:
WAREHOUSE NOTICE - Closed for stock count

The Frankfurt warehouse will be closed on Monday 16 November for the yearly stock count. We first planned to count on Friday 13 November, but a large delivery is due that day, so we moved the date. No shipments will leave on the 16th. Trucks booked for that day will go on Tuesday 17 November instead, and Sofia will contact every carrier. If your order is urgent, tell Lucas by Thursday 12 November, and he will check whether we can send it earlier.

Liam, Warehouse Manager

questions.q: How many days after the first planned count date is the new one?
options: 3 days
4 days
5 days
2 days
questions.explanation: The count moved from Friday 13 November to Monday 16 November.

questions.q: Why was the stock count moved?
options: Several carriers asked for a quieter Monday
The warehouse team did not have enough staff
Some trucks needed the first date for urgent loads
A big delivery was expected on the planned day
questions.explanation: The notice says a large delivery is due on 13 November, so the date was moved.

questions.q: What should someone do if their order cannot wait until 17 November?
options: Let Lucas know by 12 November
Call Sofia on the day of the count
Ask Liam to open the doors on the 16th
Phone the carrier directly on Monday
questions.explanation: Urgent orders must be reported to Lucas by Thursday 12 November.

title: New price list in December
text:
SUPPLY ALERT: New price list from 1 December
Norvia Packaging will update its price list on 1 December. Orders placed and paid by 28 November keep the old prices, even if delivery is in December. Orders placed after that date, or paid later, follow the new list, which is on average 4% higher. Standing orders move to the new list automatically. Please send questions to Hannah Berg at the Södertälje site, who will reply within two working days.

questions.q: Which statement is correct?
options: An order placed and paid on 25 November keeps the old price.
Every order delivered in December gets the new price list.
Standing orders keep the old list until they are cancelled.
Orders paid by 28 November will cost 4% more than before.
questions.explanation: Orders placed and paid by 28 November keep the old prices, whatever the delivery month.

questions.q: How soon will questions be answered?
options: On the very same day
Within two working days
By the end of November
Once the new list starts
questions.explanation: Hannah Berg will reply within two working days.

title: New launch date
text:
LAUNCH NOTICE: New date for the Singapore launch

The launch planned for Monday 16 November will now take place on Monday 30 November. The regulator asked for one extra document, so approval is now expected on Wednesday 25 November. Mateo will update the supply plan, and Hannah will tell customers about the new date. Please send your revised forecasts to Mateo two working days before the supply review on Thursday 19 November. No new stock should be ordered until approval is confirmed.

questions.q: Why was the launch postponed?
options: A supplier is late with the first batch of product.
Forecasts were sent to the wrong colleague by mistake.
An authority needs more paperwork before approving.
The supply review has moved to a later week.

Send updated forecasts before the review meeting.
Inform customers about the new launch date.
Give their revised figures to Mateo.
questions.explanation: Hannah, not the readers, will tell customers about the new date.

options: Forecasts must reach Mateo by Tuesday 17 November.
Forecasts are due on Thursday 19 November, the day of the review.
Approval is expected before the original launch date.
Hannah will update the supply plan with Mateo.
questions.explanation: Two working days before Thursday 19 November is Tuesday 17 November.

title: Temporary label supplier
text:
SUPPLY NOTICE - Temporary supplier for item LB-204

Because of a press breakdown, our usual supplier cannot deliver label stock LB-204 until 27 November. Until then, orders may go to Kestrel Print, but only if the quantity is under 5,000 units; larger orders must wait for the usual supplier. Aisha will approve all Kestrel orders, and Fatima in the Singapore office will update the price list. Kestrel's lead time is 6 working days from the order date.

questions.q: Which statement is NOT true?
options: Kestrel Print can supply orders of any size
Aisha approves the orders placed with Kestrel
The usual supplier should be back by 27 November
Fatima updates the price list

options: Aisha
Fatima
Noah
The usual supplier

options: Tuesday 17 November
Wednesday 18 November
Thursday 19 November
Friday 20 November
questions.explanation: Six working days after Wednesday 11 November is Thursday 19 November.

title: Extra customs declaration
text:
Customs update: additional import declaration

Dear partners,

From Monday 1 February, shipments entering the Czech Republic from outside the EU will need a second electronic declaration describing the goods' final destination, on top of the standard entry form. The authorities introduced it after several consignments were cleared under the wrong tariff code, which distorted duty collection. We appreciate the extra paperwork and have no wish to burden you. That said, please confirm by Friday 22 January that your brokers can file it: a consignment arriving without it will be held at the border, with storage fees falling to the shipper. Since a held trailer also blocks our pallet returns, we are asking now.

Pavel Horak
Prague service centre, Ostrava Pallets

questions.q: Why did the authorities introduce the second declaration?
options: Border queues had become far too long.
Storage fees were not being paid on time.
Some goods were misclassified.
Pallet returns had gone missing in transit.
questions.explanation: The text says consignments were cleared under the wrong tariff code.

questions.q: What is the writer's real concern in sending this message?
options: Border delays could hurt his own operations.
He wants to discourage partners from importing.
He doubts that the new rule will really apply.
He wishes to criticise the authorities' decision.
questions.explanation: He explains that a held trailer also blocks Ostrava Pallets' returns, which is why he asks now.

questions.q: What should partners do by 22 January?
options: File the second declaration with the authorities themselves.
Pay the storage fees for held trailers in advance.
Reclassify their goods under a different tariff code.
Say whether their brokers are able to file the extra form.
questions.explanation: The writer asks partners to confirm that their brokers can file the declaration.

title: New label, old stock first
text:
NOTICE: New labels on 250 ml bottles

From Monday 3 November, Solano Plastics will print bottles with the updated label. Staff must keep using old-label stock first, until it runs out. New-label pallets go to a separate area, Bay 4. Correction to yesterday's note: it is Bay 7, because Bay 4 is being repaired. We expect the old stock to be used up by the end of the tenth working day, counting 3 November as day one. Priya will mark the new pallets, and Chloe will update the inventory system. Questions go to Greta.

To explain how to handle stock during a label change
To ask staff to repair the racks in Bay 4 this week
To report a quality problem with a plastics supplier

Monday 3 November
Friday 14 November
Thursday 13 November

questions.q: Which statement is NOT true?

Chloe will update the inventory system.
Priya will mark the new pallets.
The new pallets will be kept in Bay 4.

title: Lot stock check
text:
STOCK CHECK - Lot 24-0713
Please check your stock of Lot 24-0713 and report the quantity by Thursday 5 November, 17:00. Jonas in Guadalajara will collect all reports. Do not open any boxes unless the outer label is damaged. If you have no stock of this lot, you do not need to send a report. Marta will contact only the offices that report more than 20 pallets. Questions go to Sofia.

Marta
Sofia
Each office manager

Reporting if you hold any of the lot

An office with no stock still has to send an empty report

title: Damaged carton on arrival
text:
QUALITY NOTIFICATION QN-2291
Site: Södertälje | Reported: Thursday, 14:20

What happened: Pallet 7 of delivery D-5530 arrived with a crushed corner on the outer carton. The inner packs look intact, but their seals have not been checked.
Impact: Pallet held in quarantine; no stock released.
Immediate action: Lucas must photograph all four sides before the pallet is moved. Sofia will decide on release only if the photos show no tear in the inner packs; if the packs are affected, Tomasz, as carrier contact, must file a claim instead.
Deadline: photos by 16:00 on Friday.

options: Stock from the pallet was released before the check
Lucas will file the claim with the carrier
Release depends on the photos showing intact packs
The delivery was refused at the gate
questions.explanation: Sofia decides on release only if the photos show no tear in the inner packs.

title: Wrong quantity booked

What happened: On Monday, Tomasz booked 1,200 boxes of leaflets into the system. The delivery note said 1,020; two digits had been swapped.

Hannah
Chloe
The supplier

The delivery note showed 1,200 boxes.
The booking was fixed on Tuesday.
The stock was counted in the warehouse.

title: Lot quarantine request

text:

During receipt of lot VL-5530, the outer carton label showed 24 units per case, while the delivery note and the pallet label both said 12. The count confirmed 12. title: Short shipment of film
text:
Deviation DV-2291: Short shipment
On Tuesday the Cork plant received 18 pallets of film against 20 on delivery note DN-7745. The carrier had first planned 22 pallets, but the order was cut to 20 on Monday. Production is not affected, because safety stock covers the gap. Samir is checking whether two pallets were left at the supplier's yard. We will not raise a claim until he confirms the count; Noah will keep the next truck booking on hold meanwhile.

options: Twenty-two, as first planned
Twenty, after Monday's change
Eighteen, as counted at the gate
Two, the amount still missing
questions.explanation: The delivery note shows 20; 22 was the old plan and 18 was received.

questions.q: In the text, what does 'safety stock covers the gap' mean?
options: extra stock hides the problem from the customer
reserve pallets are stored beside the missing ones
the carrier pays for the shortage with its own stock
spare inventory is enough to make up for the shortage
questions.explanation: Safety stock is the buffer that means production is not affected.

questions.q: Why is the plant not raising a claim yet?
options: The shortage is too small to justify any claim.
The supplier has already promised to pay.
It wants to confirm the pallets are missing.
The delivery note is considered unreliable.
questions.explanation: It will not raise a claim until Samir confirms the count.

title: Shorter expiry on delivery
text:
Quality notification QN-3318

On Thursday the Frankfurt warehouse received batch L2207 from Tessaro Materials. The agreed shelf life on arrival was at least 12 months, but the label shows only 9 months. title: Cracked vials report
text:
Supplier Nonconformity Report SNR-3051
Supplier: Pellegrini Glassworks. Location: Frankfurt warehouse.

During incoming inspection on Monday, 12 of 400 vials from batch GL-88 showed hairline cracks. The lot has been placed on hold while you investigate. Camille (Quality) leads on our side; Jonas (Planning) should be contacted only about replacement dates, and not copied on technical findings.

Required: a written root-cause analysis by Wednesday 18 November. We would rather not escalate this, but a repeat of the March issue would leave us little choice.

options: Sent back to the supplier as soon as possible today
Counted again by the warehouse team before any decision
Kept aside and not used until a decision is made
Released for normal use together with a warning label

To tell the supplier about a late payment on an earlier invoice
To announce a new inspection procedure for all incoming goods

Indifferent to whatever the supplier decides to answer back
Convinced that the supplier caused the cracks on purpose

title: Repeat label misalignment
text:
Trend note QN-2291: misaligned carton labels

Three similar deviations were reported this month on packing line 2. On 6 October, 12 cartons carried labels that sat slightly off-centre; 9 more followed on 15 October, and 15 on 27 October. None left the building, and no customer impact is expected. The cause is unconfirmed, although a worn applicator head is the leading suspect. Samir will inspect it by Friday 30 October, and Yuki asks that nobody adjusts the line settings meanwhile. Frankly, three repeats in a month is not something we can keep calling coincidence.

questions.q: What does the final sentence suggest the writer believes?
options: The events are too minor to need any follow-up.
Samir caused the problem by changing settings.
Customers will soon start complaining.
The repeats probably share one root fault.
questions.explanation: Saying it can't be called coincidence implies a common cause.

questions.q: In the text, what does "leading suspect" mean?
options: The person most likely to be blamed
The part that is easiest to repair
The cause that has been confirmed
The most probable explanation
questions.explanation: The cause is unconfirmed, so the worn head is only the likeliest explanation.

questions.q: Which statement is NOT true?
options: The labels were off-centre on three separate dates.
Samir will examine the applicator head.
More than 40 cartons were affected in total.
None of the affected cartons were shipped.
questions.explanation: 12 + 9 + 15 makes 36 cartons, not more than 40.

title: Late batch record review
text:

title: Missing analysis certificate

title: Conditional lot release
text:
DEV-0418 - Lot 7H2 conditionally released

Following the temperature excursion reported on 2 November, the additional checks came back within limits, so Mateo has signed off the lot for release on Wednesday 11 November. The release comes with strings attached. First, the lot may ship only to the two customers who have already accepted the deviation. Second, every pallet must carry a remaining-shelf-life check before dispatch, which Elena's team will log in the system. Third, if a single complaint comes in within 30 days, the lot goes back on hold pending review. Nadia has asked that nobody treat this as a precedent; the checks were thorough, but she would rather not repeat the exercise. Questions to Nadia, Södertälje site.

title: Incomplete batch record signatures
text:

During the review on Tuesday 10 November, 6 of the 40 batch records sampled had no operator signature. Fatima Ortiz, the auditor, welcomed the fact that the team fixed two records on the spot, but she expects the rest to be closed two working days before the management review on Friday 20 November. title: Batch on hold
text:

Until then, the batch must not be shipped or allocated to customer orders. Planners should mark it as unavailable in the system and look for other stock for any order due before Monday. title: Returned pallets inspection
text:
Quality notification QN-7702 - Returned goods inspection
Background: A customer in Poland returned 18 pallets of sealed vials on Monday, citing suspected temperature excursions in transit. Rafael completed the inspection at the Warsaw distribution centre the same day. Findings: data-logger readings showed that 12 pallets stayed within range throughout. Of the remaining six, four exceeded the upper limit for under thirty minutes, which falls within the tolerance agreed with the carrier; the other two breached it for over two hours. Disposition: the 12 compliant pallets and the four marginal ones may be restocked once Ingrid has countersigned the log; the other two are to be written off. Dev will raise the claim against the carrier and chase it until credit is issued. Until sign-off, all returned stock stays segregated.

handed back to the carrier for a credit note
counted again by Rafael at the end of the month
kept apart from other stock
questions.explanation: Returned stock is held separately until sign-off.

title: Year-end timesheets and holidays
text:
Subject: Year-end timesheets and holiday planning

Hi everyone,

A quick reminder before the year closes. Timesheets for December must be submitted by Friday 18 December, and I can only approve holiday requests for the first week of January once your timesheet is in. Please also let me know which days you plan to take between Christmas and New Year, so we can make sure the desk is covered.

I'll do my best to say yes to everyone, but the end-of-year close has to come first. If two people want the same days, I'll go by who asked first.

Thanks,
Greta

title: Year-end stock counts

title: New weekly report time
text:
Subject: New time for the weekly report

Hi team,

From next week, please send your weekly report on Thursday at 12:00, not on Friday. The regional managers now meet on Friday mornings, and they want the numbers before the meeting. Send it to Jonas as usual, unless you are on holiday that day. In that case, ask Chloe to send it for you.

title: Why the reports differ
text:
Subject: Why the two stock reports disagree

Hi Elena,

The 4,860-pallet figure in the warehouse report and the 5,130 in the finance one are both right, as it turns out; they simply count different things. The warehouse report only includes pallets that have been put away, whereas finance also counts goods received but still on the dock. The 270-pallet gap is therefore largely a matter of timing.

I would rather align the cut-off times than change either report. Could you get Andrés's agreement no later than two working days before Thursday's planning review, so that I can adjust the templates in time?

Greta

Obtain Andrés's agreement by Tuesday
Raise the matter for the first time at Thursday's review

title: New approval for large orders
text:
Subject: New approval step for purchase orders above 25,000 euros

Dear team,

As of Monday 2 November, any purchase order above 25,000 euros will need a second signature from Liam before it goes to the supplier. The change follows the audit in September, which showed that several large orders had gone out with a single approval. Requests should be submitted at least two working days before the date you need the order placed. Anything below the limit follows the usual route. Please check your open drafts today and resubmit any that exceed it.

Jonas

Thursday 5 November

Suppliers complained about repeated and duplicate orders
The old limit had been set far too high by mistake
An audit found large orders approved by one person

Cancel all orders that are under 25,000 euros

title: Purchase request sent back
text:
Subject: PR-5530 returned - licence renewal
Hi Noah,
I've had to send your purchase request back, and I'd like to explain why before it looks like a flat refusal. The renewal is above the 5,000 euro threshold, which normally requires two quotes; a single quote is accepted only if the vendor is the sole supplier, and the request doesn't show that. That's no criticism of the need itself, which is clear.
Once you've added either a second quote or a short note confirming sole-supplier status, resubmit and I'll approve it within a day. Omar in procurement can issue that note; I can't write it for you.
Thanks,
Tariq, Finance Partner

He accepts it is justified.
He suspects the vendor is overcharging.
He is annoyed it was submitted late.

Describe the business need again in more detail

title: Training on the new planning tool
text:

Omar

title: Recurring coating shortage
text:
Subject: Recurring shortage of film-coating material - escalation

Dear Marta,

I am writing to escalate the third shortage of film-coating material this quarter. Each time, the supplier has promised delivery but then pushed back the date, and our buffer stock has run dry before the replacement arrived. Last time we had to expedite a shipment at our own cost.

I would like to propose a meeting with the supplier's director. Could you confirm your availability by Monday? The S&OP review is on Thursday 19 November, and I would like the agreement in place two working days before it, so I can include the new lead time in the plan.

Best regards,
Jonas

The buffer stock ran out before the replacement arrived
The order was much larger than the forecast had predicted

title: Demand review decisions

Subject: Is the October forecast firm or indicative?
Dear Sofia,
Thank you for the forecast you shared last month. Before we order raw material, I need to know how to treat it. If the first eight weeks are firm, we will buy now and carry the risk ourselves up to your agreed tolerance of 15 percent. If the whole forecast is indicative, we will wait for purchase orders, which would push the earliest delivery from week 45 to week 48. Could you tell me which applies by Thursday, so that we can lock the plan? A short call would be welcome, but only if that is easier than writing back.
Kind regards,
Liam, Ridgeway Cold Chain, Singapore office

To ask for a wider tolerance.

title: Price increase and volume discount
text:
Subject: Rates from 1 January - and a way to soften them

Dear Noah,

I'm writing ahead of the January rate review to be upfront about a change. Our reefer transport rates will rise by 5 per cent, mainly because fuel and driver costs have outpaced what we can absorb. I appreciate this is not what you wanted to hear.

That said, we'd like to keep the Barcelona to Rotterdam lane competitive. If you commit to at least 200 pallet movements per quarter, we can offer a 5 per cent volume discount on the new rate, applied at quarter end as a credit rather than on each invoice. For reference, your current rate is €80 per pallet, and you moved 180 last quarter.

Happy to talk it through whenever suits.

Warm regards,
Priya
Ridgeway Cold Chain

questions.q: What would Noah effectively pay per pallet if he meets the volume condition?
questions.explanation: €80 plus 5 per cent is €84, and a 5 per cent discount on €84 gives €79.80.

to keep the message short and informal
to be polite but deliberately vague
to sound firm and demanding about it
questions.explanation: She states the increase openly and admits it is unwelcome news.

Noah already met the volume condition last quarter.
Fuel and driver costs are behind the increase.
The condition is 200 pallet movements a quarter.
questions.explanation: Noah moved 180 pallets last quarter, below the 200 needed.

title: Please keep the noise down
text:
Hi Tomasz,

I hope you're well. I don't want to be the neighbour who complains, so please take this as a friendly nudge rather than a grievance. I have an important video interview on Wednesday 19 November, from 6 to 8 PM, and the walls between our flats are not exactly thick.

Would it be possible to keep the music down during those two hours? I'm not asking you to cancel your band rehearsal, just to skip the drums. If that really can't be done, drop me a line two working days before, by Monday, and I'll borrow a meeting room at work instead.

Thanks a million,
Nadia

title: Focus hours policy
text:
Focus hours policy - Frankfurt warehouse
To give staff uninterrupted time for deep work, no meetings are held from 09:00 to 11:00 on Tuesdays and Thursdays. Shift managers may book a meeting in this time only for safety issues. Other teams should offer slots after 11:00, and requests that ignore this rule can be declined. Questions go to Samir.

To say when meetings are not allowed

Eleven hours
Four hours

title: Gifts from suppliers
text:
Policy: gifts from suppliers

Employees may accept small gifts worth up to EUR 30, such as a pen or a box of sweets. Anything more valuable must be declined politely. If a gift arrives by post and you cannot return it, tell your manager within two days and hand it to Ines in Compliance, who will decide what happens to it. While a tender with that supplier is open, no gift may be accepted, whatever its value, because it could seem to influence the decision. Questions: ask Pavel.

the supplier who sent it

Ines, in Compliance

a payment that is made in advance

The gift would be counted as taxable income.
questions.explanation: The text says it could seem to influence the decision.

title: Raising a concern anonymously
text:
Raising a concern anonymously

You may report a concern without giving your name through the Speak Up form on the intranet. The form does not record your address, and reports are read only by the Compliance team, so line managers are not involved at the start. This is because people are more likely to speak up when they know their manager will not see the report.

Compliance will acknowledge your report within two working days and give you a case number. If you want to add information later, quote that number; without it, we cannot link your messages. Investigations normally start within ten working days of the acknowledgement. Questions about the process can go to Hannah or Dev in Compliance.

Because Compliance also handles payroll for the company
So that employees feel safe to raise problems
Because managers must stay neutral during every audit

Ask for a review of one's salary

text:
Expense claims: limits and deadlines

text:

If a European fare is above €400, the traveller's manager must approve it first, and only then will the travel desk issue the ticket. Exceptions for urgent customer visits need the department head's written approval. Flexible fares should be chosen only when plans are likely to change. Questions? title: Absence handover policy
text:
Absence and handover policy
Since 1 October, anyone absent for more than three working days must set an out-of-office message and complete a handover note. Previously the threshold was five days; that rule no longer applies. The note names a deputy, lists open items by urgency and states how to reach you in a genuine emergency. Notes must be uploaded to the team folder by the last working day before leaving. Where the absence is unplanned, for example through illness, the line manager completes the note within one working day of the absence starting. Absences of three days or fewer need only an out-of-office message. Questions go to Hannah in HR Operations; Tomasz in IT can help with auto-reply settings.

title: Parking and shuttle rules
text:
Parking and shuttle - Singapore office

From 1 December, parking permits for the basement car park will be issued only to staff who have registered their vehicle plate in the online form. We would appreciate it if you could do this by Thursday 26 November; permits are cancelled automatically if no plate has been entered. Spaces are allocated on a first-come basis, with the exception of reserved bays for visitors and disabled drivers. The free shuttle, open to all staff, runs every 15 minutes between the office and the nearest MRT station from 07:30 to 09:30 and from 17:00 to 19:00. Questions go to Yuki at the front desk.

text:

title: Annual leave rules
text:

Employees may carry over up to five unused days into the next year. Days beyond that expire on 31 December. We kindly ask that all requests for the first quarter reach your manager by Friday 4 December, so that cover can be planned over the holiday period. Requests received afterwards are considered only if cover allows. Approved days must be taken before 31 March, otherwise they lapse. Please contact Chloe in HR if your situation is exceptional.

title: Device and password rules
text:
Device and password rules - Singapore office
From 1 July, passwords must have at least 14 characters; the old minimum of 10 no longer applies. Staff must change existing passwords within 30 days. Because lost or stolen laptops were behind most of last year's incidents, every device must be encrypted and lock itself after five minutes of inactivity. The employee is responsible for reporting a lost device within two hours; IT Security will then wipe it remotely. Software updates install automatically and need not be reported. Contact Lucas for exceptions.

title: Keeping orders and invoices
text:
Policy: keeping orders and invoices

Purchase orders and supplier invoices must be kept for seven years after the end of the financial year in which they were created. Our financial year ends on 31 December. Paper copies are scanned by the Frankfurt warehouse office and then shredded; the scanned file is the official copy. Warehouse staff do not decide what to delete. Only Finance, led by Samir, may delete records, and only after the seven years have passed. If you are unsure whether a document counts as a record, ask Noah before you throw it away.

title: Overtime and time off
text:
Overtime approval and time off in lieu

Overtime must be approved by your line manager before it is worked, except in an operational emergency, in which case approval must be requested within one working day afterwards. Approved overtime is entered in the timesheet system by the employee and then confirmed by the manager.

Compensation is given as time off in lieu at 1.5 hours for each hour of approved overtime. It can be booked once the manager has confirmed the timesheet entry, and must be taken within three months; hours not taken by then lapse, unless the manager agreed a later date in writing. Payroll, not the manager, handles any cash payment, and only for staff on grade 2 or below.

For questions, contact Samir in HR Operations. Yuki coordinates the Södertälje timesheets.

title: Working from home rules
text:

You may work from home up to two days a week. Core hours are 10:00 to 15:00, when you must be available. Tell your manager the day before. For a third day, you need written approval from Marta at least three working days ahead. Beatriz in HR can answer questions. text:

If you see a problem with a product or process, report it within 24 hours. Use the online form on the intranet. Your shift supervisor does not fill in the form for you, but Samir in Quality checks every report. Hannah's team starts the investigation only after Samir has accepted the report. If the problem could affect a delivery, also phone Ingrid at once.

title: Purchase approval thresholds
text:
Purchase approval - thresholds
Requests up to 5,000 euros are approved by the budget holder alone. Between 5,001 and 25,000 euros, the request also needs sign-off from the finance controller, Nadia Ortega. Anything above 25,000 euros goes up the chain to the regional director, who may sign only after the controller has reviewed it. Please do not split a purchase into smaller orders to stay under a limit; this practice, known as 'salami slicing', is not permitted and will be flagged during audits. Because delays at this stage hold up production, the controller has committed to respond within two working days. Emergency repairs are the exception: the plant manager may authorise them verbally, provided the paperwork follows within three days. Marta in Procurement can answer questions.

approving purchase requests more slowly
splitting one purchase into small ones
paying suppliers a long time in advance

Large requests are rather rare in the plant

questions.explanation: Only purchases above 25,000 euros go to the regional director.
